name: Memo
useWhen: Use this for a short notice to people inside your workplace, school, or group.

sections.label: To / From / Date / Subject
sections.what: Four lines: To, From, Date, and Subject.
sections.tip: Type each label, a colon, then the detail. One per line.
sections.good:
To: All Front Desk Staff
From: Jordan Reyes, Office Manager
Date: October 28, 2026
Subject: New time sheet deadline

sections.label: Purpose
sections.what: The main point, first: Bottom Line Up Front.
sections.tip: Readers skim memos. The first sentence should tell them what changed or what to do.
sections.good: Starting Monday, Nov 2, all time sheets are due by 5 p.m. Friday.
sections.bad: I wanted to share some thoughts about time sheets.

sections.label: Background
sections.what: Short context: what led to this.
sections.tip: Two or three sentences. Skip it if everyone already knows.
sections.good: Payroll moved to a new system in October. It needs the weekend to process checks.
sections.bad: So basically a lot of stuff happened.

sections.label: Details
sections.what: The facts people need: dates, times, places, who it affects.
sections.tip: Short sentences. A new paragraph for each new topic.
sections.good: Submit time sheets in the Payroll app. Payroll pays late time sheets the following week.
sections.bad: Do the time sheets the normal way but different.

sections.label: Action needed
sections.what: What each reader must do, and by when.
sections.tip: One clear action with a date. Say who to ask with questions.
sections.good: Please submit this week's time sheet by 5 p.m. Friday, Oct 30. Questions? Email Dana at payroll@example.com.
phrases: You don't need to do anything unless…

topics.name: General
topics.tone: Brief and businesslike. Main point first.
dos: Put the main point in the first sentence
Say who to ask with questions
donts: Add a greeting or sign-off (memos don't use them)
Bury the action at the end of a long paragraph

topics.name: Policy Change
topics.tone: Clear and neutral. Explain what changes and when.
dos: Name what's different from the old way
Explain why in one or two sentences
donts: Leave out who it applies to

details.tip: Show the old rule and the new rule side by side.
details.good: Old: time sheets due Monday at noon. New: due Friday at 5 p.m.

topics.name: Meeting Notice
topics.tone: Practical. Make it easy to show up prepared.
dos: Give day, date, time, and place
Say what the meeting is for
Say what to bring or read first

details.tip: List the when, where, how long, and what to bring.
details.good: When: Thursday, Nov 5, 10–10:30 a.m. Where: Conference Room B. Bring: your Q3 numbers.

topics.name: Announcement
topics.tone: Upbeat but professional. Share the news in plain words.
dos: Say the news in the first sentence
Say what it means for the reader
